ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $15.21 Ryde voucher refund (NS-7) for the combined 10.79 km of unexempted detour across both segments; no account action against the driver.

segment_findings.reason: Code-settled: no exemption candidate applies. The 21:26 KPLY accident is one incident on the optimal corridor and does not explain a segment deviating up to 2,240 m off route; the driver's statement cannot supply the RD-4(a) link because system records outweigh statements, and no RD-3/RD-5 exemption exists [F3][F13][F10][RD-1][RD-4].

Code-settled: the only incident record (F13) is tied to the optimal route and does not explain a 22:04–22:13 deviation drifting up to 931 m off route; band 4/5 records are corroborative only, and there is no rider-named stop or prior rider consent, so the 3.85 km is chargeable under RD-1/RD-2 [F4][F13][F14][RD-1][RD-2][RD-4].

rejected_claims.reason: Rejected in part: it asserts both segments are covered by no exemption, but its own concession concedes the 21:26 KPLY accident is a reasonable cause for the first stretch; more importantly its premise of two fully unexempted segments understates the refund — the code-settled trace leaves both segments unexempted, giving $15.21, not the $5.43 the rider asks for [F3][F4][F13][RD-1][RD-2][RD-4].

The $16.41 upper-bound alternative is rejected: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segments' extra km at the metered rate and excludes the ≤0.25 km matching residual between the fare excess and the sum of the segment extra km, so the refund is 10.79 km × $1.4099 = $15.21 [F1][F3][F4][F5][F7][RD-2].

Rejected as a basis for any independent finding: duration alone (F2) is not an off-route fact and RD-1 sets no time or percentage threshold; the liability rests on the two recorded gps segments, not on the +20.4 min [F2][F3][F4][RD-1].

Rejected as an exemption ground: RD-4(b) band records are corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment standing alone; bands 4 and 5 never reach band 1/2, so both segments remain chargeable under RD-4(c)/RD-2 [F11][F12][F3][F4][RD-4][RD-2].

Rejected as a defence for either segment: absence of a chat route agreement does not exempt a driver-initiated deviation — RD-5 requires the driver to propose the change before leaving the optimal route and the rider to expressly agree, which the record lacks [F8][F9][F10][RD-5][RD-3].

Rejected as a full defence: that no rider-directed stop exists (F8, F9) only confirms RD-3 grants no exemption, leaving both segments to be tested under RD-4, where they fail for want of incident evidence explaining the substituted stretches [F3][F4][F13][RD-3][RD-4].

Rejected as understating the remedy: the driver's advocate's $5.43 figure covers only segment F4, but the code-settled trace leaves F3's 6.94 km unexempted as well, so RD-2 yields 10.79 km × $1.4099 = $15.21 [F3][F4][F5][F7][RD-2][RD-4].
